---
title: Workspace storage RLS
description: Path-scoped Row Level Security for the workspaces Storage bucket, its regression matrix, and the tested rollback.
---

## Access model

The `workspaces` bucket stores objects as `<wsId>/<root>/...`. Supabase Storage
enforces `storage.objects` RLS for browser and user-token clients. Owning server
APIs use the service role, which bypasses RLS. Migration
`20261026100000_least_privilege_workspace_storage_rls.sql` replaced the original
policies. Those let any workspace member read, write and delete every object.

All rules require a `MEMBER` workspace membership (`is_org_member`; guests are
excluded). `public.workspace_storage_object_access(name, operation)` evaluates
them:

| Root | select | insert / update | delete |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat/<chatId>/**` (legacy AI attachments) | chat creator | none | chat creator |
| `chats/ai/resources/<chatId>/**` | chat creator | none | chat creator |
| `chats/ai/resources/temp/<userId>/**` | that user | none | that user |
| other `chats/**` (native Chat), `external-apps/**`, `AI Agent Imports/**`, `mira/images/**`, `recordings/**`, `.tuturuuu/**` | none | none | none |
| `project-updates/**` | member | member | member |
| `template-backgrounds/**` | member | `manage_drive` | `manage_drive` |
| everything else, including root-level files (Drive) | `view_drive` or `manage_drive` | `manage_drive` | `manage_drive` |

- Private roots match case-insensitively and never fall back to Drive permissions.
  `AI Agent Imports` contains spaces; the match uses the literal segment.
  `drive/mira/qr/**` (QR codes saved to Drive) stays a Drive object; only
  `mira/images/**` is private.
- Names containing empty, `.` or `..` segments are denied.
- Clients cannot write private roots. Chat uploads use
  `POST /api/ai/chat/upload-url`, which checks membership and chat ownership
  before it issues a signed upload URL. An existing chat must belong to the
  caller. An id that does not exist yet is allowed for draft attachments.
- Meeting recording routes check membership and the recording session, then use
  the service role for storage. Playback signs only paths inside the verified
  session folder.
- `project-updates` keeps member access because its task route still uses a
  request-scoped client. Move it to a service-role route before tightening it.
- The private-root list follows the Drive private upload census in
  [Drive](/platform/applications/drive). Add new private roots to the helper,
  the Drive path policy and the test matrix together.

RESTRICTIVE `workspace_storage_guard_*` policies enforce the same helper on every
command. The legacy `Enable insert for authenticated users only` policy
(`WITH CHECK (true)`) can no longer widen access to this bucket. Before this
migration, it let non-members insert into any workspace folder.

## Regression coverage

`apps/database/supabase/tests/workspace-storage-least-privilege-rls.sql` covers
15 objects across every root. Each is probed by a non-member, a member, a
`view_drive` viewer, a `manage_drive` manager, the chat owner/uploader and
`service_role`, for select/insert/update/delete. With 8 structural checks, that
is 368 assertions. Each probe runs in a rolled-back subtransaction.

Route tests in `apps/web/src/__tests__/mind-chat-file-app-session-route.test.ts`
cover the upload-url and delete-file ownership checks.

## Verify on a disposable stack

Run this on a remote devbox only, never on the shared laptop. Copy
`apps/database/supabase` to a scratch directory and give `config.toml` a unique
`project_id` and free ports. Then, from `apps/database`:

```bash
ttr resources run -- node scripts/run-supabase.js --workdir "$SCRATCH" start
ttr resources run -- node scripts/run-supabase.js --workdir "$SCRATCH" \
  test db supabase/tests/workspace-storage-least-privilege-rls.sql
```

Stop it afterwards with `stop --project-id <id> --no-backup`.

## Rollback

`apps/database/rollbacks/20261026100000_least_privilege_workspace_storage_rls.rollback.sql`
restores the exact 20231004102905 policies and drops the helper. It does not
touch objects. Rolling back reopens the HIGH finding, so run it only as an
approved incident rollback.

To prove the rollback round trip on the disposable stack:

1. Apply the rollback file with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`.
2. Run `apps/database/verification/workspace-storage-rls-rollback-roundtrip.sql`.
   It runs 7 assertions: the old policies are back, the new ones are gone, prior
   member-wide semantics apply, and objects are untouched.
3. Re-apply the forward migration body in a transaction.
4. Re-run the 368-assertion test.

The migration sets `lock_timeout = '5s'` and `statement_timeout = '30s'`. Its
policy DDL takes only a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on `storage.objects`. If
the lock is not acquired in 5 seconds, it fails without partial changes; retry
it.
